title: Legal Personal Assistant
description:
Personal Assistant (Private Client)
- Location: Leatherhead
- Job Type: Full-time
- Salary: £30-£32,000

Join a leading law firm in the Southeast known for its strong history and commitment to client service. We are looking for a Personal Assistant to support our Private Client team, ensuring optimal efficiency and contributing to our tradition of excellence.

Day-to-Day of the Role:
- Provide direct support to a team of four Private Client solicitors/fee earners, alongside two other part-time secretaries.
- Prepare correspondence and documents through audio-typing and word processing.
- Manage daily filing and the maintenance of client files in accordance with office procedures.
- Prepare mail and enclosures for dispatch and handle all copying needs.
- Schedule appointments, arrange meetings, and maintain up-to-date diaries for fee earners.
- Set up and clear conference rooms for meetings and provide refreshments as needed.
- Offer support to other secretaries and provide guidance to junior and temporary secretaries.
- Engage with clients both in person and over the phone in a professional and friendly manner.
- Maintain confidentiality of all firm and client documentation and information.
- Operate the firm's case management system and undertake online form filling requirements.
- Continuously seek to improve the efficiency of the department and undertake additional duties as required.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Substantial previous legal secretarial experience, including at least 2 years in Private Client work.
- Advanced IT skills in relevant packages and fast touch typing skills.
- High levels of accuracy and professionalism in communication.
- Proactive approach to work, able to progress client matters without supervision.
- Ability to work to deadlines, cope under pressure, and effectively prioritise workloads.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, sensitive to the needs of clients during distressing times.
- Demonstrates commitment to the firm and a genuine interest in legal work.

Benefits:
- Competitive salary with annual reviews and bonus schemes.
- 5% employer pension contribution and Death in Service benefit of 4x salary.
- Private medical cover, Life Assurance, and Company sick pay.
- Cycle to Work scheme, Employee Assistance Programme, and Health and Wellbeing initiatives.
- 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays, with enhanced maternity/paternity leave and other leave benefits.
- Flexible/hybrid working options, sabbaticals, and study leave.
- Comprehensive opportunities for personal and professional development including a Trainee Solicitor Programme and extensive CPD programme.

To apply for this Personal Assistant position, please submit your CV and cover letter detailing your relevant experience and why you are interested in joining to Mark Watts at Reed, your Local Legal Recruitment Manager.

title: Crisis Prevention Support Worker
description:
Reports to: Client Services Manager

Hours: 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday, between 8am-6pm. Flexible working arrangements available for the right candidate. Hybrid working is also available.

Salary: £28,325 per annum. Fixed Term to April 2029.

About York Road Project

York Road Project is a homelessness charity based in Woking, supporting people experiencing homelessness for over 30 years.

York Road Project exists to defeat homelessness. Through our Today Centre, Tonight Centre and Tomorrow Houses, we work alongside people to prevent homelessness, respond to crisis, and support long-term recovery and independence.

Purpose of the Role

York Road Project is a partner in the Woking Crisis Prevention Consortium, which brings together local organisations to help residents build resilience, improve wellbeing and prevent issues from escalating into crisis.

Working alongside Welcome Church, Woking Foodbank, Citizens Advice Woking, Barnardo's and Home-Start. The Prevention Support Worker will provide intensive, person-centred support to adults experiencing multiple disadvantage and complex needs. Working with individuals for up to 12 months, the postholder will help identify and address issues at an early stage, build resilience and independence, and reduce the likelihood of future crisis through coordinated support and partnership working across the Woking Crisis Prevention Consortium.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage a caseload of approximately 20-22 individuals annually.
- Undertake holistic assessments to identify strengths, needs, risks and goals.
- Develop and review person-centred support plans.
- Provide practical and emotional support tailored to individual circumstances.
- Build trusting relationships that encourage engagement and positive change.
- Deliver support in community settings, individuals' homes and other appropriate locations.

Prevention and Resilience
- Identify emerging issues and intervene before they escalate into crisis.
- Support individuals to improve financial stability, wellbeing and independence.
- Help people strengthen support networks and reduce isolation.
- Encourage the development of skills and confidence to manage future challenges.
- Promote long-term stability and reduce reliance on crisis services.

Partnership Working
- Receive and make warm referrals within the consortium.
- Work closely with consortium partners to coordinate support around individuals.
- Signpost and refer to specialist services where appropriate.
- Attend multi-agency meetings and advocate for clients when required.

Monitoring and Evaluation
- Maintain accurate case records and support plans.
- Record all client contacts, interventions and outcomes.
- Complete regular reviews to monitor progress and adapt support where required.
- Contribute case studies, outcome reports and monitoring information for funders and consortium partners.
- Support the evaluation and ongoing development of the service.

Professional Practice
- Participate in supervision and training
- Contribute to service improvement and shared learning across the consortium.
- Work in accordance with safeguarding, confidentiality and data protection requirements.

Person Specification

Essential
- Experience of supporting adults with complex or multiple support needs.
- Experience of managing a caseload and delivering one-to-one support.
- Understanding of issues such as poverty, housing insecurity, poor mental health, substance misuse, offending behaviour and social isolation.
- Ability to undertake assessments and develop support plans.
- Experience of partnership and multi-agency working.
- Strong communication, organisation and record-keeping skills.
- Understanding of safeguarding adults.
- Ability to work independently and use sound judgement.

Desirable
- Experience of prevention or early intervention services.
- Experience within homelessness, housing, social care or community support.
- Knowledge of trauma-informed and strengths-based approaches.
- Knowledge of local support services and referral pathways.
- Experience of delivering wellbeing or mental health support.
